solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Portrait of interest to police stolen from among mine (8)

indicatorNotes.among: HOT and OF sit among the letters of PIT

blocks.note: hot = stolen, as hot goods are
of = from, as in a man of Kent

annotation.surface: A detective hunting a painting lifted from a mine owner's collection.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'Portrait' a stolen artwork; it is the police's own picture, a face built up from a witness's description. A Photofit is the British name for this identikit picture.
annotation.definitionFit: A Photofit is a likeness assembled to help police find a suspect, so it is a portrait of interest to them.

entries.clue: PC in house moved to higher level predictive text (9)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' in its plain place sense: COP is to be found inside ROSE

blocks.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
a PC (police constable) is a cop

annotation.surface: Someone upgrading the text-prediction software on their home computer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'PC' and 'predictive text' both push you towards computers; PC is a police constable, and the predictive text is the stars' forecast in the paper.
annotation.definitionFit: A horoscope is a written forecast, so it is text that predicts.

entries.clue: May baby possibly start to appreciate nature rambling? (7)

indicatorNotes.rambling: NATURE wanders into a new order

annotation.surface: A child born in spring encouraged to enjoy country walks.
annotation.walkthrough: Taurus runs from about 20 April to 20 May, so a baby born in May may well be a Taurean; 'possibly' covers the ones born after the 20th.
annotation.definitionFit: A Taurean is someone born under Taurus, which covers much of May.

entries.clue: Dashing sailor with loud orange coat on (11)

indicatorNotes.on: in a down clue, F and RUST are placed on top of RATING

blocks.note: rust is the orange coat that forms on iron
a rating is an ordinary sailor

annotation.surface: A dashing sailor in a loud orange jacket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dashing' looks like a description of the smart sailor; it is the verb, as in dashing someone's hopes.
annotation.definitionFit: Dashing hopes is frustrating them, so both mean thwarting.

entries.clue: Carpet / which parasite victim might want to get? (4,3)

annotation.definition2: which parasite victim might want to get?

blocks.note: to carpet someone is to tell them off

blocks.clueFragment: which parasite victim might want to get?
blocks.note: read literally: a tick is a bloodsucking parasite, and its victim wants it removed

annotation.surface: A dog owner wondering what a flea-ridden pet would want.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Carpet' as a verb means to reprimand, from being called on to the carpet in front of the boss. The second half reads the phrase literally.
annotation.definitionFit: To tick someone off is to scold them, which is what carpeting them means.

entries.clue: Recognized perch from the rear flap (6)

indicatorNotes.from the rear: read SAW SIT from its back end

annotation.surface: A bird spotted on its perch from behind.
annotation.walkthrough: Tiswas is British slang for a state of agitation, as in 'all of a tiswas'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in British informal use: both name a state of nervous agitation, usually said of someone 'in' one.

entries.clue: Ballerina’s support, on point (3)

blocks.note: on = to, as in fixing one thing on or to another

annotation.surface: A dancer balanced on the tip of her foot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On point' is exactly where a ballerina stands, so the wordplay seems part of the definition; it splits into TO and a compass point.
annotation.definitionFit: A ballerina dancing on point is held up by her toes.

entries.clue: Has Cnut ordered halt mid-flow? (7)

indicatorNotes.ordered: the letters are put into a new order

annotation.surface: King Cnut commanding the tide to stop coming in.
annotation.walkthrough: The legend has King Cnut (Canute) ordering the tide back; 'ordered' is the anagram signal hiding inside that story.
annotation.definitionFit: To staunch a flow of blood is to stop it while it is running.

entries.clue: Gulf [of] America next to southern edge of States (5)

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for America
the S at the edge of States

annotation.surface: The Gulf of America, the recent renaming of the Gulf of Mexico, on the southern US coast.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface borrows the new name for the Gulf of Mexico; 'Gulf' is simply a chasm.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: beside its sea sense, gulf also means a deep chasm or yawning gap.

entries.clue: Dutch brought back through Jaguar factory (4)

indicatorNotes.through: the answer runs through the words

blocks.note: the run of letters jagUAR Factory

annotation.surface: A Dutch person returned to a car plant.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' is not the nationality: 'my old Dutch' is Cockney for a wife, and Frau is German for wife.
annotation.definitionFit: Dutch means wife in Cockney slang, and a Frau is a wife.

entries.clue: Dirty half of yard in which five play (5,5)

indicatorNotes.in which: 'in which' places what follows inside what came before, so five sits within the word for dirty

blocks.note: V is five in Roman numerals

annotation.surface: Five children playing in a muddy corner of a garden.
annotation.walkthrough: 'play' is the noun: Chekhov's Uncle Vanya.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Chekhov's 1899 drama of a disappointed estate manager is one play among many.

entries.clue: Terms of Endearment remade, so new The Sting? (5,8)

indicatorNotes.remade: the letters are made again in a new order, like a film remade

annotation.surface: Hollywood remaking one Oscar winner, so the new version is The Sting.
annotation.walkthrough: Terms of Endearment and The Sting are both Oscar-winning films, which makes 'Terms of Endearment' read as a title; here it means loving words.
annotation.definitionFit: Sweet nothings are the affectionate words lovers murmur, terms of endearment.

entries.clue: Spooner’s hammock rocking violently (11)

indicatorNotes.Spooner’s: swap the opening sounds of two words, as Reverend Spooner did

blocks.note: a hammock is a bed hanging between two supports
trade the opening sounds of the two words, B for H, and say what comes out

annotation.surface: Someone swinging hard in a hammock.
annotation.walkthrough: Headbanging is shaking the head violently to rock music; 'rocking' is both the hammock's swing and the music.
annotation.definitionFit: Headbanging is thrashing about to rock music, so rocking violently.

entries.clue: Clear skin that’s surprising close to your ears (6)

indicatorNotes.to your ears: what you hear, not what is spelt

blocks.note: cor! is an exclamation of surprise; near = close

annotation.surface: A remark about a spotless complexion seen up close.
annotation.walkthrough: Cor is a British exclamation of surprise. Said in a British accent that drops the final R, cor near sounds like cornea.
annotation.definitionFit: The cornea is the clear outer layer over the front of the eye.

entries.clue: Thrash unknown, entertaining mum with great show (8)

indicatorNotes.entertaining: to entertain is to host a guest, so FLAIL takes SH inside it

blocks.note: to flail is to thrash about
mum = silent; sh! calls for quiet

annotation.surface: A party thrown for mum by someone who knows how to put on a show.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mum' is not mother but the mum of 'keep mum', saying nothing.
annotation.definitionFit: Doing something flashily is doing it with great show.

entries.clue: Beauty fascinated by sounds (5,4)

blocks.note: to be into something is to be keen on it

annotation.surface: A beauty entranced by music.
annotation.walkthrough: 'sounds' is a verb: to sound out, to investigate, as a surgeon sounds a wound.
annotation.definitionFit: To sound a matter is to probe it, which is to look into it.

entries.clue: Ten asses’ worth of silver rani’s due after trading (8)

annotation.surface: An Indian queen owed ten donkeys' worth of silver after a deal.
annotation.walkthrough: An as was a small Roman bronze coin; the silver denarius was worth ten of them. 'asses' is there to be read as donkeys.
annotation.definitionFit: The denarius was the Roman silver coin originally valued at ten asses.

entries.clue: British papers in time put into reduced format (7)

indicatorNotes.in: 'in' in its plain place sense: British papers are found inside time

blocks.note: an age is a period of time
BR is an abbreviation for British

annotation.surface: British newspapers switching to a tabloid format in good time.
annotation.walkthrough: 'papers' suggests newspapers and 'reduced format' tabloids; the papers are identity documents.
annotation.definitionFit: To abridge a text is to shorten it, putting it into a reduced form.

entries.clue: Promising some tennis, not cricket? On the contrary (3,4)

blocks.note: a set is a unit of a tennis match
'not cricket' means unfair, so its contrary is fair

annotation.surface: A forecast of tennis rather than cricket for the summer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'It's not cricket' is a British idiom for unfair play; 'on the contrary' flips it to fair. Set fair describes settled weather.
annotation.definitionFit: Weather that is set fair is promising, likely to stay fine.

entries.clue: Polish brought west to fight make dugouts? (6)

indicatorNotes.brought west: in an across clue, west is leftward, so RUB is read backwards

annotation.surface: Polish troops sent west to dig trenches for the fight.
annotation.walkthrough: The capital P makes 'Polish' the nationality; it is the verb, to shine.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: burrowing is digging a hole to shelter in, and a dugout is exactly such a dug shelter.

entries.clue: Final part manufacturer has sent from the same stock (7)

indicatorNotes.Final part: take the last letter of manufacturer

annotation.surface: A maker shipping the last component from existing stock.
annotation.walkthrough: 'sent' is not dispatched but the older sense of transported with delight.
annotation.definitionFit: Relatives come from the same family stock.

entries.clue: I see complications involving trigonometry — [that’s] normal in maths (2,5,6)

indicatorNotes.involving: to involve once meant to wrap up or enfold, so AH enfolds TRIG

annotation.surface: A student grasping that trigonometry is full of complications.
annotation.walkthrough: In maths a normal is a line perpendicular to a surface, so 'normal' here is a noun-like technical sense, not ordinary.
annotation.definitionFit: A technical sense: in geometry 'normal' means perpendicular, so a normal line meets a surface square on.

entries.clue: What replaced Clay, for instance? (5)

annotation.surface: A question about what took the place of clay.
annotation.walkthrough: The boxer Cassius Clay took the name Muhammad Ali, a new name replacing the old one, which is what an alias does.
annotation.definitionFit: An alias is a name taken in place of another, as Ali replaced Clay.

entries.clue: Language unit struggling with Danish (10)

indicatorNotes.struggling: the letters thrash into a new order

annotation.surface: A language unit in a course where learners find Danish hard.
annotation.walkthrough: Hindustani is the everyday language of north India and Pakistan, spanning Hindi and Urdu.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the lingua franca of north India and Pakistan, it is one language among many.

entries.clue: Capital of Peru really Lima (3)

blocks.note: so = really, as in so good
Lima is L in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A geography fact: Peru's capital is Lima.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Capital' is money, not a city: the sol is Peru's currency. Lima, Peru's actual capital, is the phonetic-alphabet L.
annotation.definitionFit: The sol is the currency of Peru, its capital in the sense of money.

entries.clue: Belt to put in loops and tighten around (4)

indicatorNotes.around: to turn around is to face the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: to knot is to loop and pull tight

annotation.surface: Instructions for fastening a belt.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Belt' looks like the thing being knotted; it is the verb, to hit. Tonk is British slang for hitting hard.
annotation.definitionFit: To tonk a ball is to belt it, hit it hard.

entries.clue: One of those cases that blow up enormously (2,4)

annotation.definition: One of those cases that blow up

blocks.clueFragment: One of those cases that blow up
blocks.note: an artillery round: a metal case packed with explosive
an intensifying phrase, as in 'hot beyond measure'

annotation.surface: Something about legal cases that balloon enormously.
annotation.walkthrough: The letters split two ways: A SHELL and AS HELL, which is why the enumeration is (2,4).
annotation.definitionFit: A shell is a casing packed with explosive that blows up.

entries.clue: Trouble getting into costume and performing dance (8)

indicatorNotes.getting into: ADO gets into the join between RIG and ON

annotation.surface: The trouble of getting into costume before going on to dance.
annotation.walkthrough: The rigadoon is a lively old French dance in duple time.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the rigadoon, a brisk Provençal dance of the 17th century, is one dance among many.
